speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our assessment, could you describe the onset and progression of your symptoms, and do you have any known history of neurodegenerative disorders, stroke, or heavy alcohol use? Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty with speech or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk-like" appearance of your gait is a crucial clue. You mentioned clumsiness is worse on the right side—can you tell me if you have noticed any specific balance issues when turning around or walking in the dark, and do you experience any visual disturbances like double vision or loss of depth perception? Also, regarding your history, do you have any family members who were diagnosed with similar neurological conditions at a young age?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.
